_decision: railW = 54px. Approved: match the origin Rail Sidebar rail width at 54px, rather than using bidezine's own Sidebar primitive collapsed-rail width of 48px. This is therefore a deliberate, recorded divergence from a bidezine value — not a case of reusing one — which is why the number is worth guarding mechanically: nothing in bidezine's own token set would produce 54 if it were ever lost.
_note: Anchored to the rail column itself (the dark rounded surface holding logo, nav track and footer), not to a button inside it. 54 is the column's border-box width; it carries p-2 (8px) padding, so its content box is 38px — exactly one rail button wide, which is what makes 54 and F-2's 38 consistent rather than coincidental.

checks._why: Asserting the padding alongside the width is what makes this check fail if someone keeps the 54 but changes the padding — that would move every rail button inside it without altering the number this row is about. The content lane is the derived consequence: 54 - 8 - 8 = 38, exactly one rail button wide, which is what makes F-1's 54 and F-2's 38 consistent rather than a coincidence. Confirmed live: clientWidth 54, contentWidth 38, and the column's first child measures exactly 38.
checks._corrected: The first version of this check asserted width: 38px, on the assumption that getComputedStyle().width reports the CONTENT box. It does not here: this element is box-sizing: border-box (Tailwind preflight sets it globally), and Chrome returns the border-box width, 54px. The runner caught it — a genuinely wrong expectation produced a FAILING evidence row rather than a passing one, which is the property M2 exists to have. Recorded because the mistake is easy to make in either direction and the failure mode is a silently wrong assertion, not an error.
